solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old PM, bluff character from Wuthering Heights

parts.note: Edward Heath was British Prime Minister 1970-74
a bluff is a steep headland or cliff face

explanation.surface: A former prime minister is likened to a brusque figure out of Emily Brontë's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bluff' looks like an adjective (blunt, hearty) describing the PM, but here it is the noun for a steep cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: The brooding anti-hero of Emily Brontë's novel is the foundling adopted by the Earnshaws.

clue.text: Note limb on insect is graceful

parts.note: E is a musical note
a leg is a limb
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An insect's limb, seen up close, is admired for its poise.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both describe something stylish and pleasingly refined in form or movement.

clue.text: Bleep, perhaps from time unit

parts.note: one is a unit, the number 1

explanation.surface: A beep emitted at the passing of each unit of time, like a clock's pip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the bleep as one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleep is an example of a single electronic sound, as from a dial or signal.

clue.text: Bent or put right round top of vase

indicators.note: the remedy word goes round, enclosing, the letter taken from the vase

parts.note: to cure something is to put it right

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone straightens out a bent vase, or puts a band round its rim.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something bent has a curve rather than running straight.

clue.text: I've a partner that's disabled

definitions.meaning: split as I'M (I am) and a word for coupled up, it describes someone who has a partner

explanation.surface: Someone declares their partnership as a way of explaining incapacity.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the run-together letters as I'M PAIRED, a way of saying 'I have a partner'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both describe a person or faculty weakened or damaged in function.

clue.text: Truffles? There's great pleasure to be had with good one

parts.note: fun is great pleasure or enjoyment
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gourmet extols the delight of eating a good truffle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows truffles are just one example of the definition; they also suggest chocolates.
explanation.definitionFit: Truffles are an example: edible underground mushrooms, members of that kingdom of organisms.

clue.text: Opportunity to wind up university head

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' tells you to write the word for wind from bottom to top

parts.note: to roll something up is to wind it

explanation.surface: A chance to wrap up business, or to finish off the head of a university.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities the title of the ceremonial head is this office, a usually honorary role.

clue.text: Char caught missing old fat?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
someone who has lost the fat they used to carry is leaner

explanation.surface: A charwoman is caught out having shed her former weight.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is a British term for a woman hired to clean houses; it also suggests burning or a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a char, short for charwoman, is a domestic employee who scrubs and tidies homes.

clue.text: Company urged to keep motorway contracted

indicators.note: the word for urged holds, keeps, the motorway letter inside it

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A firm was pushed to keep a motorway under contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' looks like a business term, but it means squeezed smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something squeezed into a smaller space has been made more compact.

clue.text: Be sparing with power to move slowly

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
to inch along is to move slowly

explanation.surface: Advice to use energy economically, creeping along to save it.
explanation.walkthrough: To pinch pennies is to be frugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to scrimp or economise is to spend as little as possible, as in pinching pennies.

clue.text: Average chap consumes Ecstasy

indicators.note: the word for chap swallows, consumes, the drug letter

parts.note: a man is a chap
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An ordinary bloke takes the drug Ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in mathematics the arithmetic average of a set of numbers.

clue.text: Second printing of book brings incitement to disorder

parts.note: an edition is one printing of a book

explanation.surface: A book's reissue stirs up public unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: speech or action urging people to rebel against the state.

clue.text: Re-rope it after damaging door curtain

indicators.note: the letters of the rope phrase come out of the damage rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to rerope a door curtain once it has been damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A loanword from French for a heavy drape hung across a doorway.

clue.text: Share address, but not a ring at the start

indicators.note: the ring letter is left out of the speech word
says the ring letter dropped is the one at the front

parts.note: an oration is a formal address or speech
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Hand out a speech, though without a ring at the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a fixed allowance or portion given to each person.

clue.text: Weak charge leaked away, mostly

parts.note: a fee is a charge

indicators.note: all but the last letter of the leaking word is used

parts.note: something that bled has leaked away

explanation.surface: A battery's weak charge has mostly drained off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both mean lacking strength or force.

clue.text: Street fighter runs into one shouting

indicators.note: the runs letter goes into the shouter word

parts.note: a bawler is someone who shouts
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A street fighter charges at someone yelling at him.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who scraps in rough, noisy fights, as in a pub or street.

clue.text: Design benefitting rug

parts.note: for means in favour of, benefitting
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: A pattern created to benefit a rug's appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the layout or arrangement of something, as of a page or document.

clue.text: Lion's out, running for way out?

indicators.note: the letters run about and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lion has escaped and is running about looking for an exit.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows 'way out' means an answer to a problem, not an exit.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an answer to a problem is a way out of the difficulty.

clue.text: Appearances in bordello ok, somehow

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words of the phrase

explanation.surface: Keeping up appearances in a brothel is somehow fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone's appearance is how they seem to others, their outward features.

clue.text: Shopping centre entirely chasing millions

indicators.note: the word for entirely comes after, chasing, the millions letter

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million
all means entirely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A shopping centre is wholly devoted to pursuing millions in profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an enclosed precinct of shops is a mall.

clue.text: Margin shown centrally in ledger

indicators.note: the central letters of the account-book word are used

explanation.surface: An accountant's margin is recorded in the middle of the ledger.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the border or rim of something, as in a page margin.

clue.text: Old, in what's not quite a record, run off to marry

indicators.note: the old letter goes inside the shortened record word
the record word loses its last letter

parts.note: an elpee is an LP record, the letters spelt out as a word

explanation.surface: An old couple, nearly breaking a record, run away to wed.
explanation.walkthrough: ELPEE (the letters LP spelt out) loses its final E to give ELPE, and O goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to elope is to go away secretly with a lover to get married.

clue.text: Sacked elder MD who is always interfering

definitions.note: a phrase describing a person, standing for a noun meaning one who is always interfering

indicators.note: the letters are ransacked, thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A senior managing director was fired for constantly interfering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacked' looks like dismissal from a job, but signals the letters being shaken up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a busybody who pokes into other people's affairs.

clue.text: Girlfriend, perhaps, knitted the sweater

indicators.note: knitting works the wool into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girlfriend has knitted a jumper as a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A girlfriend is an example of a beloved, a term of endearment for one's partner.
